lines.text: The drain under the arch was older than the Order. Aldric's own channel, Tamsin said, running from the old spring out to the tunnels. The water came up to our knees, then our waists.
Nell rode on Ash's back, holding his ears like reins. Oswin leaned on Wren and bled, and complained, which was a good sign.
If I die in a drain, tell everyone it was a wyrm.
Behind us, torches. Then voices. Then the clank of armour in the water. Caddoc's Hounds were coming, and they were faster than a wounded knight and a frozen lord.
Where the old channel met the aqueduct tunnels, the roof came down low, into one narrow arch of crumbling brick. Above it, worn almost smooth, was the carving of the king with no rings.
We went through. Ash didn't.
He stopped under the arch, turned around, and stood there, filling it. The frost of her hand still glittered on his head.
Ash! No! Not again! Come!
He looked back at me once. Just once. The way he had looked at me in the ruined kennel, the day I found him. As if I were the only thing in the world.
Then he faced the dark, and the torches, and the Hounds.
I tried to go back. Wren held one arm. Oswin, bleeding, held the other. Tamsin put herself between me and the arch. I think I hit somebody. I don't remember who.
It's only a dog! Burn it!
Caddoc's fire came down the tunnel like a burning river. Ash met it head on.
The old arch couldn't take it. Its bricks had held for three hundred years. They gave way all at once, in a roar of stone and water and fire.
The last thing I saw was a pair of amber eyes in the firelight, between me and everything that wanted me. Then the tunnel was gone.
I reached for his thread. I had felt it every day since I named him. Thick and warm and always there, lying on my feet.
I couldn't find it. Not cut. Not gone. Just lost, somewhere in the dark under Aldcrown.
We came up out of the aqueduct shaft at dawn, into the Lowmarket. Mags was waiting there with her buckets, as if she had known. She took one look at my face, and didn't ask.
Across the city, a new thread crackled like a fire catching. My brother was alive. Ilse was free. Nell was asleep in her sister's arms. We had done everything we came to do.
Ash wasn't with us.
And before the sun was fully up, every bell in Aldcrown began to ring.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and nine, coming soon.
